title: Turn an Idea into a Specification

learn.title: Agree before building
learn.body: An idea names a possibility; a specification describes the software well enough to judge the result. Write it before asking AI to code. This gives both of you a shared target and makes omissions easier to spot while they are still cheap to change.

learn.title: Start with a person
learn.body: A user story connects a person, a need and a reason: as a habit tracker user, I want to check off a habit so that I can see today's progress. It describes value, not a button layout or a database choice. Add other stories only when they serve a distinct need.

learn.title: Set boundaries and define data
learn.body: List what is in scope, what is explicitly out of scope and what information must be stored. A first version might include habits and one completion per calendar date, while excluding accounts, syncing and reminders. Clear non-goals stop a small request from becoming an unplanned product.

learn.title: Decide what done means
learn.body: Discuss edge cases before implementation: a repeated tap, an empty habit name, a new calendar day or unavailable storage. Then write acceptance criteria as observable outcomes. For example, after checking off Read and reopening the app, Read appears complete for that same date.

learn.title: Specify the first habit check-off
learn.body: Turn the broad idea of a personal habit tracker into one buildable slice.
steps: Idea: help me follow a few daily habits without making setup complicated.
Story: as a user, I want to check off a habit so that I can see today's progress.
Scope and data: store a habit name and completions by date; exclude accounts, syncing and reminders.
Edges: a second tap does not duplicate completion, blank names are rejected and a new day starts incomplete.
Acceptance: after I check off Read and reopen the app, that date still shows Read complete exactly once.

learn.body: Ask AI to identify assumptions and unanswered questions in your draft. You choose the answers: a fluent specification can still describe the wrong product.

questions.prompt: Which detail belongs in an initial specification?
choices: The observable result the user should get
A guarantee that generated code will be correct
The exact wording the AI must use in its reply
questions.explanation: A specification defines the desired behavior and constraints. It is a target for building and checking, not a guarantee about generated code.

questions.prompt: A \_\_ connects a person, a need and a reason.
questions.explanation: A user story explains who needs something and why. This keeps the work focused on user value rather than jumping straight to implementation.

questions.prompt: Match each specification part to its job.
pairs: States what this version will not include
Describes an observable result to check
questions.explanation: These parts answer different questions: value, boundaries, stored information and evidence of completion. Together they reduce ambiguity.

questions.prompt: Put this early design process in a useful order.
steps: State the idea and intended user value
Set scope and define the necessary data
Decide how important edge cases should behave
Request an implementation for the agreed slice
questions.explanation: Behavior and acceptance criteria give implementation a target. Deciding them after coding makes it easier to mistake convenient output for intended behavior.

questions.prompt: What is the two-word term for observable statements used to decide whether a requirement is done?
questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria state outcomes that can be observed and checked. They make done a shared decision rather than a matter of confidence.

questions.prompt: The draft says users can check off a habit but says nothing about repeated taps. What should happen before coding?
choices: Decide and record whether repeated taps create one completion or several
Let the AI choose silently because repeated taps are an implementation detail
Add social accounts so there is a more complete first release
Wait until users report a problem before discussing the case
questions.explanation: Repeated taps affect stored data and visible behavior. The specification should resolve this edge case so the implementation and checks share the same expectation.
